transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date/Time: 2026-03-12 16:00 PT
- Duration: ~45 minutes
- Attendees: Sara Patel (Redwood AE), Diego Morales (Redwood SE), Michael Grant (Orion CISO), Priya Raman (Orion Head of Compliance), Jared Lee (Orion Cloud Infra), Aisha Khan (Orion Procurement)

Summary: quick posture review of SOC2 & ISO artifacts, Trust Center navigation, KMS/encryption options, RBAC/SSO, audit logs, data residency, and next steps to provide controls mapping.

Topics: Trust Center & artifact access, SOC 2 Type II scope, ISO cert details, controls mapping, RBAC/SSO + SCIM, audit logging retention and access, KMS/HSM integrations, Private deployment networking, demo/benchmarks for PII redaction flow.

Action items (recap at end of call included): see action_items field.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Sara: hey everyone thanks for joining, this is Sara from Redwood, i'm the AE on the account, um we also have diego from solutions engineering, he'll run through the detailed controls and k yes?
[00:12] Michael: hey Sara thanks, Michael here, CISO at Orion, couple of us on the call today to understand your SOC2 and ISO posture and how we'd get artifacts and mapping.
[00:20] Priya: hi all, Priya, head of compliance. main concerns: evidence for access controls, encryption at rest keys, and audit log retention for at least 7 years for some of our regulated flows.
[00:33] Sara: great thanks, we'll start with a high-level then diego will go into specifics. quick note, i'll share the Trust Center link after the call with the redacted SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 certs.
[00:45] Diego: hi everyone, Diego here. quick agenda: SOC 2 scope/timeframe, ISO certificate, RBAC and SSO options (SAML + SCIM), audit logs and retention, KMS integration options for Private deployments, and controls mapping.
[01:05] Jared: one clarifying q — when you say KMS integration, do you mean Redwood's hosted KMS or bring-your-own KMS via HSM/KMS? we need BYOK for some workloads.
[01:15] Diego: yes we support both patterns. for Hosted API we use a managed encryption approach; for Private deployments we have integrations for customer-managed KMS (AWS KMS, GCP CMEK, Azure Key Vault) and HSM gateways. there was a small typo in our public docs earlier — people saw "Redwood Dedicate" in one place — ignore that.
[01:33] Michael: ok, good. can you confirm whether SOC 2 Type II covers the hosted platform and the control period?
[01:42] Sara: our latest SOC 2 Type II covers the period Jan-Dec 2025, and it covers the hosted API and the Redwood Console operations. Private deployments are covered in some control mappings but customers are responsible for infra controls in their VPC. i'll share the exact scope in the doc.
[01:58] Priya: and ISO 27001? we need the certificate and the statement of applicability.
[02:05] Sara: yep we'll include the ISO 27001 certificate and the SOA in the Trust Center. the SOA has the list of implemented controls — diego will point to where the evidence links are.
[02:15] Diego: for controls mapping, we maintain a spreadsheet that maps SOC 2 controls and ISO Annex A to our internal control IDs and evidence artifacts in the Trust Center. we'll export that for you and highlight which controls remain customer-managed for Private installs.
[02:33] Michael: what's your typical retention window for audit logs in hosted? is there an extended retention add-on?
[02:40] Diego: hosted default is 90 days for detailed request logs and 12 months for aggregated metrics. we do offer extended retention as an add-on (1, 3, 7 years) via our observability add-on — there are different storage tiers and pricing. note: per-call transcripts are separate and have their own retention policy, we'll include that.
[02:58] Priya: 7 years is non-negotiable for some of our reporting, so we'll need the add-on. will that be covered under contract?
[03:06] Sara: yes that's discussable — procurement can add the observability retention package to the contract. Aisha from procurement is on the call if we want to tag that.
[03:14] Aisha: yes we will need a pricing sheet but that is fine, we'll review after we get the SOC/ISO artifacts.
[03:20] Jared: on RBAC — can you map roles to our internal roles? we need fine-grained role assignments and audit trails for role changes.
[03:28] Diego: Redwood Console supports RBAC with role templates (admin, operator, viewer), and we also support custom roles. role changes are captured in audit logs with timestamp and actor; we also integrate with SSO/SAML and support SCIM for automated provisioning. some transcripts of older calls show "K-V cash" when we talk about KV cache optimizations, so ignore that mismatch in docs.
[03:49] Michael: good, and if we do private deployment in our VPC, what's in-scope for Redwood vs Orion? we need a clear split for the auditors.
[03:58] Diego: good question — generally Redwood is responsible for the application layer software, runtime, and service side controls we ship; Orion is responsible for customer-managed infra: VPC network configuration, KMS keys, host patching, OS hardening, and any third-party services in your VPC. we'll flag those in the controls mapping spreadsheet with clear owner column.
[04:16] Priya: evidence of configuration management — will you provide baselines or images?
[04:22] Diego: for Private installs we provide hardened image recipes and a set of recommended CIS-like baselines. we can provide a list of artifacts: image checksums, deployment runbooks, and configuration templates. some customers require runbook-level evidence for the auditor — we can surface that.
[04:36] Michael: about encryption-in-transit and at-rest — what's default and what changes with BYOK?
[04:42] Sara: default: TLS 1.2+ in transit, AES-256 at rest with provider-managed keys for hosted. BYOK means you control the key lifecycle — we integrate with AWS KMS/GCP CMEK/Azure and we can show how keys are used to wrap data keys. Diego will show a diagram in the follow-up deep dive.
[05:00] Jared: do you support hardware-backed HSM (FIPS 140-2 Level 3) for encryption?
[05:06] Diego: we support customer HSM gateways and can integrate to FIPS-validated HSMs depending on the cloud provider; we documented that in the Trust Center but i'll include a pointer.
[05:16] Priya: auditors will ask about change management and patching cadence — do you have an SLA and patch windows documented?
[05:24] Sara: yes, our change mgmt process and patching cadence are documented in our policy artifacts. for hosted we have maintenance windows and rollback plans. for Private installs we provide the recommended cadence and can share evidence of recent patches.
[05:35] Michael: there's a question about data residency — we operate in eu-west-1 for euro customers, can you guarantee regional isolation and controls?
[05:44] Diego: hosted customers can choose region-specific deployments; we offer regional tenancy and data residency controls. Dedicated and Private provide stronger guarantees since you can pin capacity or deploy in your VPC. we'll add region-specific SLA language if needed.
[05:57] Priya: we also need to know about third-party subprocessors and subservice orgs — is there a list?
[06:02] Sara: yes Trust Center includes up-to-date list of subprocessors and dates. We'll share that link.
[06:08] Michael: are there redaction or PII handling features out-of-the-box? we have flows that ingest customer statements with SSNs.
[06:15] Diego: Redwood has PII redaction options and a recommended pattern: client-side tokenization + server-side policy for redaction. we also offer a PII masking pipeline as part of the Private deployment where you can run additional filters before data hits the model. if you need, we can run a short benchmark for your redaction flow.
[06:31] Priya: yes please, that would be useful. auditors will want to see the pattern and how it preserves non-repudiation and auditing.
[06:39] Sara: next steps recap: i'll share Trust Center link + artifacts; diego will assemble controls mapping; jared to share network diagram; we'll schedule deep dive for KMS and Private networking.
[06:51] Michael: timeline — we'd like artifacts by end of next week to feed into our audit prep.
[06:57] Sara: that's doable, we'll aim to get the initial package by 2026-03-13.
[07:03] Aisha: procurement will need a redacted SOC2 for the contract team — please include the redacted report in the Trust Center link.
[07:11] Diego: i'll also include sample evidence links (policy docs, runbooks, image checksums). note: some folks have compared Redwood to BigCloudAI; the differentiation we often highlight is controls transparency and Private deployment options.
[07:27] Michael: ok good, sounds like a plan.
[07:30] Sara: any other open questions?
[07:33] Priya: one last one — do you provide attestations for ISO surveillance audits? basically do you agree to sign a SOC 2 letter to auditors?
[07:41] Sara: we have an auditor cooperation process; we provide a standard auditor request intake and respond to auditor inquiries per our policy. we'll include the onboarding steps for auditors in the packet.
[07:50] Michael: thanks everyone. look forward to the artifacts.
[07:53] Sara: thanks all, we'll follow up with the links and schedule the deep dive. bye.

End of transcript. Note: transcription includes occasional mis-hearings (eg "K-V cash" for KV cache, "Redwood Dedicate" typo). Participants used trade names casually (BigCloudAI, ModelServeCo).
